newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada 1996 farm net cash income falls 8.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada 1996 farm net cash income falls 8.0 pct.

text.p: Farm net cash income in Canada fell eight percent in 1996 compared to 1995 after higher operating expenses more than offset an increase in receipts on Canadian farms, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
The net cash income of farm businesses was C$5.5 billion in 1996 compared with C$5.9 billion the year before, the federal agency said.
Operating expenses jumped eight percent to C$22.9 billion, due to higher costs for feed, crop and hail insurance, land rental, fertilizer and machinery and heating fuel, StatsCan said.
Cash receipts rose five percent to C$28.4 billion, with livestock revenues leading the way.
Crops and livestock products accounted for 96 percent of total receipts in 1996 and program payments the other four percent, StatsCan said.

After adjusting for inflation, net cash income in 1996 represented only 45 percent of the record-high 1975 level. Adjusted 1996 recepts were five percent above 1975 figures, but expenses were 54 percent higher, reflecting the industry's increased dependence on purchased inputs.
The eight percent rise in farm operating expenses was the largest year-over-year gain since 1981, the agency said.
Significant increases were reported for fertilizer, crop and hail insurance premiums, feed, land rent, machinery fuel and heatin fuel.
Feed costs jumped 32 percent due to continuing high livestock inventories, StatsCan said.

For the first quarter of 1997, farm cash receipts fell less than one percent from the same quarter of 1996, to C$7.7 billion. Crop receipts declined to C$3.9 billion in the first quarter of 1997, four percent below last year's level, the agency said.
(For more information on net farm income, contact Bernie Rosien at Statistics Canada, 613-951-2441)
